main_text.head: DE REPVBLICA LOCRENSIVM in Italia.
main_text.p: Visse quoque olim in ea Italiæ parte, quam magnam Græciam prisci dixerunt, Locrensium infignem rempublicam, accepimus: quam ante Strabonem & Diodorum Siculum, & ante Polybium, vetustissimi & gravissimi autores, qui ea florente florebant, Plato & Demosthenes cum primis commendarunt. Ille namque in exordio Timæi fui, cui ex Timæo Locrensi philosopho Pytha-goreo, quem cum Socrate ac aliis de re-rum natura & mundi origine disserentem inducit, nomen dedit, civitatem hanc in Italiâ quàm optimè legibus constitutam isto tempore fuisse, & in ea Timæum genere & opibus nulli secundum floruisse, ac summos magistratus & honores cepisse, atque adeò in studiis ad eruditionis culmen adscen-disse, affirmat. Alter laudatam rempu-blicam eam haberi, & dignam esse, cujus prudentiam, atque in tuendis bene latis legibus constantiam imiten-tur

page.notes: The initial V of "Visse" is a large decorative letter, transcribed as one word. Long s (s) is rendered as plain s throughout, including "fuisse", "cepisse", "studiis", "esse", "constantiam". "disserentem" is read from the broken line "difleren-tem" and the context of Timæus; the scan is unclear there. Line-end hyphens are kept as printed. The paragraph continues on the next page with "tur" as its last word. The scan shows show-through and the edge of the neighbouring page at the left and right, which are left out.
